more.title: Artificial photosynthesis uses waste CO₂ to grow protein-rich edible fungus in seven days
more.summary: While many people think first of meat when they think about dietary protein, most protein ultimately depends on plants, since livestock feed on grass, hay and other plants. Meeting the demand for protein is taxing on the environment, requiring massive amounts of land and water while creating greenhouse gas emissions.

more.title: Certain fungi turn specialized plant cells into water-carrying cells using one protein
more.summary: Can a pathogen that causes damage to a plant also make that plant more resilient to drought? An international research team led by the University of Göttingen has investigated this apparent paradox. The researchers discovered how certain fungi promote the formation of new water-conducting cells in plants. At the same time, infected plants showed increased tolerance to drought stress.

more.title: Carbon nanotube measurements reveal quantum model better explains collective electron behavior
more.summary: An international team of scientists from Lithuania, Finland and Israel has conducted both theoretical and experimental research into carbon nanotubes, becoming the first to demonstrate which physical model governs the motion and interactions of electrons within them.

more.title: Shopping as a 'collector' makes us want to buy more, new research shows
more.summary: Shoppers are more likely to buy products and pay more for them when they adopt a "collecting mindset," according to new research co-authored by Bayes Business School (City St George's, University of London).

It is an eroded geological dome about 100 million years old created by igneous activity and uplift in the nation of Mauritania. In this type of geologic structure, rocks […]

more.title: Giant lambda-shaped stellar nursery found in the Milky Way's outskirts
more.summary: Massive stars often form in dense regions, called "hubs," where filamentary structures made of star-forming materials meet. These star-forming complexes are "hub-filament" systems. Astronomers have discovered one such large network of molecular gas filaments in the outer regions of the Milky Way. It is called the λ-complex, and the structure is bigger than most known hub-filament systems.

more.title: Heaven scent: Study shows link between a partner's body odor and sexual intimacy
more.summary: Many people spend a considerable amount of time and money trying to disguise their natural body odor. But not everyone finds our natural scent unpleasant. In fact, it could be part of what makes a couple click.

more.title: Using lunar craters as free radiation shields for moon base nuclear reactors
more.summary: Powering any future lunar base is a massive engineering challenge. The two-week lunar night can drain batteries charged by solar panels during the two-week day, if the batteries themselves can even withstand the freezing temperatures that go along with it. So, for decades at this point, engineers have planned to use a nuclear reactor to at least partially power any future human settlement on the moon.

more.title: Structural agility of 2D crystals enables digital doping of graphene superlattices
more.summary: A study published in Nature has demonstrated that applying an electric field can switch the atomic arrangement in a stack of two-dimensional (2D) crystals, accompanied by an unusual charge behavior. This provides a new experimental platform for exploring how the structural and electronic properties of atomically thin materials interact.

more.title: Do we really know more about space than the ocean?
more.summary: New discoveries are made about the world every day—a species of deep-sea fish here, a new galaxy there. There's a saying, "We know more about space than the ocean." But is this true? How do we determine knowing? Is it the number of things we have directly observed, or is it a matter of resolution?

more.title: From solving to 'digesting': How mathematicians can adapt to the dramatic changes AI has brought to their field
more.summary: Mathematics is having an existential crisis. On Nov. 20, 2026, a mathematician at the AI company Anthropic claimed that while working with the model Claude, he had solved the generalized Riemann hypothesis, the most famous problem in mathematics. This problem has stood unsolved for 167 years, and solving it could easily warrant a Fields Medal—considered equivalent to a Nobel Prize, but for mathematics.
